text:
olivia (support): FYI customer acme-inc reporting intermittent 429s + p95 token latency spikes from their dedicated eu2 pool since ~11:30 UTC. They say it looks like throttling, but p95 jumps to ~1.2s then 429s for short windows. Ticket SUP-7891 created.

ashwin (oncall): Which pool id / MIG config? Any tenant logs or example request that reproduces it?

olivia (support): Pool: eu2-dedicated-84, tenant: acme-inc. MIG config on node: mixed 1g.10gb slices (4 per GPU) — fractional packing enabled. Customer sent this curl sample showing 429s during spike:

```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": {"code":"POOL_THROTTLE","message":"request throttled due to node contention"}
}
```

oncall-bot: host-gpu-23 metrics snapshot (11:46 UTC): SM_util p95=95%, mem_bw p95=82%, slice_evictions=21/min, KV cache miss rate bumped 3x during spike.

devon (sre): Sounds like noisy-neighbor on fractional MIG packing. When sibling slices push SM/mem BW hard we see scheduler backpressure -> per-slice throttles/evictions and API 429. Can you run a short repro on the pool to confirm? Steps I usually use below.

lillian (infra): I checked autoscaler logs: scaler saw node utilization climb but aggregation window delayed trigger due to backpressure on metrics ingestion (we had gc on metrics-db). Autoscaler min_nodes=3 and target_util=0.7, current nodes=3 -> it couldn't autoscale because by policy burst requires 2min sustained. So mitigation: manual scale or enable burst_capacity.

devon (sre): Repro steps (quick):
1) run this load generator from a quiet client (8 concurrent connections):
```bash
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","prompt":"test","max_tokens":32}' &
done
wait
```
2) on host: sudo nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 to watch SM% and mem BW
3) tail inference runtime logs: /var/log/redwood/runtime/gpu-allocator.log for slice evictions and throttles
Expected: p95 latency spike and short windows with 429 + runtime log lines like `slice throttle: reason=sm_saturation sibling=3 evict_count=..`

olivia (support): I ran the load test against a staging node and saw matching logs: `slice throttle: reason=mem_bandwidth_capping sibling=2` and API returned POOL_THROTTLE. Customer confirmed same messages in their logs.

ashwin (oncall): Short-term mitigation: 1) Move acme-inc to a node with full-GPU allocations (no MIG fractional packing) — reduces sibling interference. 2) Manually scale pool +2 nodes while we investigate. 3) For longer term: tighten fractional packing policy or add per-slice QoS cap. Note: moving to full GPU increases cost and changes billing — advise customer.

lillian (infra): To manually scale: `redwoodctl pools scale --pool eu2-dedicated-84 --add-nodes 2 --reason "SUP-7891 noisy neighbor mitigation"` — I'll run that if support confirms. Also can trigger immediate tenant relocation: `redwoodctl allocations migrate --tenant acme-inc --target-policy full-gpu --force` (maintenance window recommended).

devon (sre): For postmortem collect:
- runtime logs around spike (gpu-allocator.log, runtime-trace.log)
- nvidia-smi dmon trace for the host (1s granularity)
- per-request trace ids from API gateway to map 429 times to host metrics
- autoscaler event log (scaler.log)

olivia (support): Got it. I'll ask customer to approve cost tradeoff and get permission to migrate. I've attached minimal repro artifacts to SUP-7891 and flagged as P1 for dedicated noisy neighbor.

support-bot: Created escalation SUP-7891 -> tier2 (oncall: @ashwin, infra: @lillian).

olivia (support): Quick note: customer also saw a couple of auth failures during spike (401) but those correlate with token refresh failures on their side; not seeing auth errors in gateway. I'll keep monitoring. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ashwin (oncall): I'll follow up after manual scale/migration. If we see repeated sibling evictions we should consider changing default fractional packing policy for this pool class. :mag:
